newsitem.title: USA: Woman who won't sing Happy Birthday loses job.
newsitem.headline: Woman who won't sing Happy Birthday loses job.

text.p: Cora Miller, a Jehovah's Witness, would not sing "Happy Birthday" because her religion forbids it, so she lost her job at a Mexican restaurant in Clinton, Maryland, where she worked as a waitress.

U.S. District Court Judge Benson Legg said on Tuesday he will hold a hearing this year on Miller's claim, backed by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, that Chi-Chi's Mexican Restaurant violated the federal Civil Rights Act.

Miller, 43, wants back pay and the commission wants punitive damages against Chi-Chi's for firing her after only one day on the job that she was hired for in July 1993. Chi-Chi's views singing the birthday song for customers as part of the job.
The commission found in favour of Miller last year but is going to court because Chi-Chi's still says it has broken no law.

Miller told the commission that when she told the restaurant manager her religious beliefs would not permit her to sing "Happy Birthday" to a lunchtime customer, he told her to leave and not come back. She said she told him she could wait tables or even work in the kitchen but she simply could not sing the song.
